title: Why No Quintic Formula?
question: Why can some equations be solved by a formula while most high-degree ones cannot?
hook: The answer came from studying how the roots of an equation can be shuffled.
idea: Whether an equation can be solved by radicals depends on the group of ways its roots can be permuted.

beats.prompt: Cubic and quartic equations both have root formulas built from radicals. You are asked about a typical fifth-degree equation. What does Galois theory say?

choices.label: A similar but longer formula exists for it
choices.feedback: The pattern from degree three and four tempts, but Galois theory explains why it breaks.

choices.label: No such formula exists for most equations of that size
A formula exists only when the roots are whole numbers
choices.feedback: Whole-number roots are not the criterion; the shuffling group of the roots is.

beats.explain: Galois theory shows why equations of degree four or lower can be solved this way and why most of degree five or higher cannot.

beats.prompt: Put these steps toward the unsolvability of the quintic in order
items: Ruffini nearly proves it using permutation groups (1799)
Abel publishes a proof, patching the gap (1824)
Galois submits his memoir on solvability by radicals (1830)
beats.explain: Ruffini came first in 1799, then Abel in 1824, then Galois's submission in 1830, and finally Liouville's printing in 1846.

beats.prompt: Match each mathematician to what they did
pairs: Partly solved the cubic, for one type, without publishing
Used complex numbers to solve all forms of cubic
Published a proof of the Abel–Ruffini theorem in 1824
beats.explain: Each step pushed the formula-hunt forward, until Abel showed the quintic has no general solution by radicals.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Every equation of degree four or lower can be solved by a formula using roots and arithmetic.
Degree five is only one step higher.
So a step up in degree cannot break the pattern, and all quintics must be solvable.
Therefore the Abel–Ruffini theorem must be mistaken.
beats.explain: Galois theory explains why the pattern does break: most equations of degree five or higher cannot be solved by radicals.
